A return value of 1 is interpreted as an error.  See pci_driver.
in local_pci_probe().  If you're wondering how this ever could
have worked
column2: it's because it used to be the case that only return

column1: values less than zero were interpreted as failure.  But even in
the current kernel if the driver registers its various entry
points with the kernel
column2: and then returns a value which is

column1: interpreted as failure
the driver still mostly works.  However

functions wouldn't work.  In the case of Smart Array

column3: which is why it took so long to

column1: notice.
Requesting backport to stable because the change to pci-driver.c
which requires driver probe functions to return 0 occurred between
2.6.35 and 2.6.36 (the pci power management breakage) and again
between 3.7 and 3.8 (pci_dev->driver getting set to NULL in
local_pci_probe() preventing driver remove function from being
called on rmmod.)
